text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1765432100 — spike in 429s across inference-prod. 5m rolling rate = 18% (baseline 0.5%). Service: /v1/generate, primary region us-west-2. Auto-rule: opened mitigation channel. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/inf/429-503-overview?orgId=1

Mike (oncall): saw the alert. grabbing metrics now. is this concentrated to embeddings or text gen?

GrafanaBot: top by route: /v1/generate (text) 63% of errors, /v1/embeddings 28%, /v1/re-rank 9%. Top tenants by 429 volume: tenant-alpha, tenant-gamma, sandbox-*. 95th token latency unchanged.

Elena (platform): preliminary hypothesis: KV cache miss storm + aggressive batching leading to head-of-line. can we enable short-circuit rate-sampler on the embeddings path?

TJ (sre): agree with kv cache angle. tail shows many concurrent cold keys. recommend immediate soft-rate-limit on embeddings for non-prod tenants and disable large-batch path: set FEATURE_FLAG=disable_large_batch for embeddings worker pool.

Mike (oncall): action plan: 1) toggle embeddings batching 2) apply tenant-level quota for sandbox-* and tenant-gamma 3) watch 5m rate and rollback if regressions. who can flip FF?

Elena (platform): I can flip the FF. running command now:
```bash
redwoodctl feature set disable_large_batch --service=embeddings --env=prod --reason="mitigation 1765432100"
```

Elena (platform): done. feature flag propagated to 3/4 clusters. waiting on last cluster.

Maya (support): paging incoming from tenant-gamma SRE — they're seeing ~40% of requests 429-ing. can we give them ETA?

Mike (oncall): tell them ETA ~10-15m, currently doing partial mitigations. ask them to pause bulk jobs for 20m if possible.

TJ (sre): applying soft tenant quota for sandbox-* and tenant-gamma to 25 rps using rate-controller:
```json
{"action":"set_quota","tenant":"tenant-gamma","limit_rps":25,"ttl":"15m","reason":"mitigation-1765432100"}
```

TJ (sre): quota applied. Watching.

GrafanaBot: 2m after FF + quota: 429 rate down to 11%. overall QPS dropped 14% (expected). errors concentrated now to tenant-alpha only.

Mike (oncall): tenant-alpha looks like the remaining offender. any recent deploy or config change?

Elena (platform): no deploys in last hour. I see tenant-alpha pattern: unusually long prompt prefixes spiking KV cache miss rate. suggest shadowing tenant-alpha to a compatible smaller model variant (quantized). Can do transparent routing to model-lite as fallback for 5m window.

TJ (sre): agree — route 30% of tenant-alpha traffic to model-lite for now. command: `redwoodctl route set --tenant=tenant-alpha --percent=30 --target=model-lite --ttl=10m`

Mike (oncall): routing applied. also enabling extra logging for tenant-alpha requests (sampling 1%).

Maya (support): forwarded status update to tenant-gamma and tenant-alpha: "We've applied temporary rate controls and routing changes, seeing partial recovery. We'll follow up when fully stable."

Elena (platform): quick check on latency P50/P95: P50 flat, P95 improved slightly for embeddings. token-level cost reduced for applicants.

GrafanaBot: 10m snapshot: overall 429 = 6.2% (from 18%), /v1/embeddings 2.1%, /v1/generate 4.1%. incidents: no 503s.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations in place. Severity downgraded to SEV-2. Keep channel open; plan next steps: follow up with tenant owners, consider longer-term fixes for KV cache expansion and smarter prefix caching.

Mike (oncall): handoff notes for next oncall cycle: mitigations active (FF disable_large_batch, tenant quotas for sandbox-* + tenant-gamma, 30% model-lite routing for tenant-alpha), alerts suppressed for 429 spike, follow-ups: request tenant-alpha logs, schedule KV cache capacity increase, eval bump for caching policy.

TJ (sre): leaving monitoring playbook for handoff. if 429>8% for 10m, escalate to SEV-1 and re-open mitigation.

Elena (platform): I'll open a tracking ticket: PLAT-4678 "KV cache growth and prefix caching work" and link to this thread + Grafana snapshot.

Maya (support): noted. sending customer follow-ups now.

Mike (oncall): thanks everyone. tagging @oncall-next to review handoff: @TJ please confirm you've captured runbook steps.

TJ (sre): confirmed. leaving channel.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT RESOLVE LOGGED — mitigations will remain for short TTLs, close when system stable for 30m.
